geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Practice the lessons so far, then check your answers.

Goal: I can use special right triangles and trig ratios.

  • 9.1 I can use the altitude to the hypotenuse to find similar triangles and geometric means.
  • 9.2 I can prove the Pythagorean Theorem using similar triangles.
  • 9.3 I can derive and use 45-45-90 side relationships.
  • 9.4 I can derive and use 30-60-90 side relationships.
  • 9.5 I can explain why side ratios in right triangles depend only on the angle.
  • 9.6 I can define and use tangent.
  • 9.7 I can define and use sine and cosine.
  • 9.9 I can find an angle from a ratio.
  • 9.10 I can connect slope to tangent of an angle and prove the parallel and perpendicular slope criteria with similar slope triangles (a 90 degree rotation for perpendicular).
  • 9.11 I can solve elevation and depression problems.
  • 9.12 I can choose trig or Pythagoras to solve problems.
  • 9.13 I can find triangle area as (1/2)ab sin C and extend trig to non-right triangles. (Not in 2023 IN Geometry; optional.)

slides.title: Practice: 9.7
slides.html: If sin A = 0.6 in a right triangle, what is cos(90 − A)? Find cos A.
slides.reveal: cos(90 − A) = 0.6. With hypotenuse 5 and opposite 3, the adjacent leg is 4, so cos A = 0.8.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • trig ratios depend on triangle size
  • sin(A) means sin times A
  • inverse trig is 1/sin
  • the 30-60-90 short leg is opposite the 60 degree angle
